LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyNature: What diplomacy asks of the colony's people weighs on those it goes against, and eases those it suits.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyNature_Tip: Some of what diplomacy asks goes against a colonist's nature, and it builds their strain (the heart's own, no mood of its own): the oath of fealty on the one who swears it, if proud; a truce or a pact broken on whoever struck the blow, took the captive or made the sale that broke it, if trusting; a hostage given on the hostage, if timid, and on their close kin, if warm; a youth sent away as a ward on the parents, if warm; a match pressed over their objection on the one matched, always; a challenge turned down on the champion, if proud or hot-tempered, and one faced on the champion, if timid; a season away as envoy or hostage on the one who goes, if set in their ways; haggling over a captive on the one who haggles, and on the captive's close kin among the colony, if warm; a truce with a people someone swore vengeance on, on the avenger, always. The further past where a side shows (30), the more: up to 12, 8 at least for what is felt whatever their nature, scaled as life's pressures are ("Life's ups and downs", and less when they are near breaking), within the heart's caps for the day. What suits them eases it instead: a season away eases the curious, up to 6. One act a day for each colonist. The heart's page says what they did and what would help; the colony's news tells it. An oath sworn may humble a proud one, and the same act against the same side twice within a year may change them (a word broken twice, a challenge faced twice, a second season away). Off: nothing new is felt, and what was felt drains as any strain does.
LanguageData.CC_Heart_NatureHelp: A quiet evening with friends would help.
